hits.hook: OpenAI: BioBasicsBench, a benchmark for agents doing routine wet-lab analysis (with Ligo)
hits.text:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

Accelerating biological research starts with getting the everyday work right. BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

https://t.co/wN2xLk0YeW

hits.name: Burke Holland
hits.hook: Burke Holland: honest first take on the iPhone Duo (thumbs up and down format)
hits.text:
Here are my thoughts on the iPhone Duo after a few days of use.

👎 When folded this thing is DENSE. Walking around with it in your pocket is going to require a belt.

👍 The outside display is small, but it doesn't bother me at all. What does bother me is the giant sidebar on the right that is just totally empty if the apps aren't making use of it.

👍👍 Unfolded this thing is glorious. The inner display feels somehow massive and the perfect size at the same time. Going back to a 17 Pro feels like you are using an impossibly skinny display.

👎 Apps that are not updated for the Duo are atrocious when using the Duo unfolded. Reminds me of the early days of iPad when all we had was phone apps and pixel doubling. 

👍 The crease is entirely unnoticeable when you're using the thing. 

👍 Two apps side-by-side is really nice. I don't need it that often, but when you do it feels so good to be able to just have 2 apps up at the same time.

👎👎 I miss FaceID way more than I thought I would. You take for granted how well it "just works" to authenticate you without you doing anything at all. It's jarring how much I'm constantly touching the fingerprint reader for 2-factor and passwords and keys and unlocking. It's actually a giant PITA.

👍 Battery life is phenomenal. Which is great considering iOS 27 totally killed my 17 Pro.

All in all, it's a superb device. 8/10 stars. Would recommend.

virals.name: Vivek sahu
virals.hook: AI is not one technology.
virals.text:
AI is not one technology.

It’s an entire ecosystem.

And the deeper you go, the more you realize that ChatGPT or Claude is only one layer of a much bigger stack.

At the foundation, you have:

→ Machine learning
→ Neural networks
→ Transformers
→ Computer vision
→ Large language models

Then comes the infrastructure that makes these models useful:

→ Data & knowledge systems
→ Fine-tuning
→ Prompt engineering
→ RAG
→ Knowledge graphs
→ Model serving & inference

But that’s still not the end.

The next layer is where AI starts doing things:

→ AI agents
→ Tool orchestration
→ Multi-agent systems
→ Autonomous execution
→ Memory systems
→ Self-reflection & error recovery

And then AI moves into real-world applications:

→ AI copilots
→ Personalization
→ Content generation
→ Code generation
→ Voice & video
→ Business automation

But there’s one part that becomes more important as AI gets more autonomous:

Trust.

Security.
Privacy.
Bias & fairness.
Explainability.
Human oversight.
Risk management.
Governance.
Compliance.

Because building a powerful AI system is only half the problem.

The bigger challenge is building one that people can trust, control and deploy safely.

That’s why the future of AI isn’t just about better models.

It’s about the entire ecosystem working together.

Models + Data + Infrastructure + Agents + Applications + Governance.

Most people are focused on the model.

The real opportunities may be hiding in everything around it.

Save this AI ecosystem map. It’s worth revisiting as the industry evolves.

Follow @Viveksahu1215 for more practical AI, tech & business insights.

virals.text:
Stop hunting for agent skills across scattered repos.

Agent Skill Index is a community-curated GitHub directory of agent skills, tutorials, and guides for builders working with AI coding assistants.

It helps you find skills for your workflow by separating official collections from community contributions and grouping resources by platform and task, so you can shortlist relevant options instead of browsing random repos.

Key features:

• Official collections – links to skills from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Hugging Face
• Task-based browsing – community sections cover development, testing, data, security, and more
• Agent documentation – links to skill docs for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and other assistants
• Usage guidance – platform-specific instructions show where skill files go and how to load them
• Skill authoring – a SKILL.md template and folder layout give you a starting point for your own instructions

It’s open-source (MIT license).

Link in the reply 👇

virals.text:
Firecrawl just turned its crawler into a toll booth. $75 million Series B in September, then this week Alexandria goes live with SEC filings for 8,000-plus public companies: one API call and your agent in ChatGPT or Claude can ask which biotech had a failed trial or what BlackRock bought last quarter. Convenient. It is also someone else's hosted service sitting between your agent and the data, billed per credit, and down if their servers are.

The pattern I keep seeing across every "LLM extraction" pitch from the last two years is the same expensive habit: re-reading the entire page with the model on every single pass, because nobody wants to maintain brittle CSS selectors by hand. That is the actual cost center, not the crawl itself.

I built DeepScrape around the opposite assumption. Generate the selector once with an LLM, reuse it deterministically on every subsequent scrape, and only call the model again when the page structure actually changes and the extraction self-heals. The LLM does targeted work: generate, validate, adapt. It never re-reads a page it already understands. DeepScrape also ships an MCP server, so instead of paying per credit for someone else's hosted index, you point your own agent at any site and turn it into a structured data source you query directly, no middleman billing you for access to data you could have scraped yourself.

Alexandria is a fine product for people who want financial data without touching infrastructure. For everyone building agents that need web data as a dependency, not a destination, the self-hosted, deterministic version is the one that does not hand a scraping company the meter.

outsiders.name: Vivek sahu
outsiders.hook: AI is not one technology.
outsiders.text:
AI is not one technology.

It’s an entire ecosystem.

And the deeper you go, the more you realize that ChatGPT or Claude is only one layer of a much bigger stack.

At the foundation, you have:

→ Machine learning
→ Neural networks
→ Transformers
→ Computer vision
→ Large language models

Then comes the infrastructure that makes these models useful:

→ Data & knowledge systems
→ Fine-tuning
→ Prompt engineering
→ RAG
→ Knowledge graphs
→ Model serving & inference

But that’s still not the end.

The next layer is where AI starts doing things:

→ AI agents
→ Tool orchestration
→ Multi-agent systems
→ Autonomous execution
→ Memory systems
→ Self-reflection & error recovery

And then AI moves into real-world applications:

→ AI copilots
→ Personalization
→ Content generation
→ Code generation
→ Voice & video
→ Business automation

But there’s one part that becomes more important as AI gets more autonomous:

Trust.

Security.
Privacy.
Bias & fairness.
Explainability.
Human oversight.
Risk management.
Governance.
Compliance.

Because building a powerful AI system is only half the problem.

The bigger challenge is building one that people can trust, control and deploy safely.

That’s why the future of AI isn’t just about better models.

It’s about the entire ecosystem working together.

Models + Data + Infrastructure + Agents + Applications + Governance.

Most people are focused on the model.

The real opportunities may be hiding in everything around it.

Save this AI ecosystem map. It’s worth revisiting as the industry evolves.

Follow @Viveksahu1215 for more practical AI, tech & business insights.

drafts.rides: @shanselman Windows Sandbox MCP (86,018 views) + your Copilot-clicks-your-desktop post (3,407)
drafts.text:
GitHub Copilot can click around your desktop now. Scott Hanselman just built an MCP server that spins up a throwaway Windows Sandbox in seconds.

Put those two together.

Before any computer-use agent touches the real machine with the real legacy app, let it break a fake one first. Your future self will thank you.
drafts.video_tip: Screen 20s: an agent clicks through an old desktop app inside a Windows Sandbox window, something goes wrong, the sandbox closes and a clean one opens. Caption: 'Let it break the fake one'.

drafts.rides: @github Copilot app Projects (87,772) + open session in VS Code (40,739)
drafts.text:
Projects in the GitHub Copilot app can span one repo, many repos, or no repo at all.

That last part is the Power Platform story. Half of our work lives in a solution, a Dataverse table and a Teams chat, not a repo.

Give Copilot the goal, let it run the sessions, then pick it up in VS Code when you want hands on keyboard.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 18s: a Project card fills with a solution file, a Dataverse table and a Teams thread, then a 'Open in VS Code' click carries the plan across. Caption: 'Not everything is a repo'.

drafts.text:
Simon Willison hides AI-generated PR descriptions behind a collapsed details tag. Steal this for Power Platform.

Two human sentences up top: what changed and why. Then the Copilot-written wall of text folded underneath for anyone who wants it.

Your reviewers read the first part. Nobody reads the second part. That is fine.
drafts.video_tip: Screen 12s: a giant AI-written description scrolls forever, then collapses into two plain sentences with a 'show more' arrow. Caption: 'Humans first, slop folded'.

drafts.rides: @github 5,000 concurrent agents on one repo (102,855) + @gdb security fundamentals (146,178)
drafts.text:
GitHub's new Git storage handled 5,000 concurrent agents and 7,200 pushes per second on one repo.

Meanwhile my tenant has a few dozen Copilot Studio agents and nobody can tell me who owns some of them.

Scale is coming whether we are ready or not. Owner, permissions, off switch. Boring fundamentals, still the job.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head 15s with a counter racing to 5,000 behind you, then cut to a short agent inventory list with blank 'Owner' cells. Caption: 'Scale is easy. Ownership is not'.

drafts.text:
OpenAI Devs posted one word and a video and pulled 2 million views over the weekend.

I write 400 words about Copilot Studio topic triggers and get 400 views.

So here is my version.

Tomorrow.
